purpose: Direction check for the rubric/cap confound: commonsenseqa and apigen_tool_next_action labelled with the redesigned rubrics and the level-0 cap off, so the level-0 share is a property of the rubric rather than of the cap's selection.

code.commit_note: the generator and library hashes are unchanged from 5ffd546; the commits between 5ffd546 and d7b9ab3 are note-only

corpus.note: the canonical artifact filtered to the two families, so that a two-source run does not drag the other 31 sources through selection

reading.apigen_tool_next_action: 91.4% of accepted rows sit at level 0 with the cap off, against 52% under the cap in round two. The cap was masking the collapse, not creating it.
reading.commonsenseqa: 53.7% level 0 with the cap off, against 56% in the pilot; the two runs bracket one another inside the interval, so the cap was not what produced its level-0 share either.
reading.caveat: one seeded selection of 350 states per family, one run. The interval is the Wilson 95% bound on the level-0 share at that n; at this size it rules out a return to the round-one numbers for apigen_tool_next_action and rules out nothing decisive for commonsenseqa. The eligibility rule, not this run, decides.
